h: An Admiral's Park and Dundee's Waterfront
p: Camperdown has a cracking back story. The park takes its name from the Battle of Camperdown in 1797, when Admiral Adam Duncan, a Dundee man, defeated the Dutch fleet. The grand house at its centre was built for his son, the first Earl of Camperdown, and the family's estate eventually passed to the city, giving Dundonians a huge green playground on the edge of town.

Beyond the wildlife centre, the park has a big adventure play area, woodland trails and a golf course, so it suits a whole family with different ideas about a good day out. Next door, Templeton Woods adds even more trails through mixed woodland, popular with dog walkers and runners. Bring a picnic and you can happily spend a long day here without spending much at all.

Dundee's waterfront is only a short drive away and has been transformed in recent years. The V&A Dundee, Scotland's design museum, sits in a striking building on the banks of the Tay that's shaped a little like a ship, and right beside it is RRS Discovery, the polar research vessel built in Dundee that carried Captain Scott on his first Antarctic expedition. Kids love clambering about the decks and hearing about the brutal conditions.

Tips: the wildlife centre is the easy part; the wider park is where the hours fly by, so wear comfy shoes. Dundee's weather can be breezy off the Tay, so layers are always a smart shout. It's a cracking all-weather combination of animals, history and wide open space, and it rarely feels crowded.
